caption: 37 war elephants. Over the Alps. In winter.
text: Thirty-seven war elephants. Over the Alps. In winter.

caption: In 218 BC, a Carthaginian general marched an army from Spain into Italy, the long way round, over the highest mountains in Europe.
text: In two-hundred-eighteen BC, a Carthaginian general marched an army from Spain into Italy, the long way round, over the highest mountains in Europe.

caption: Then he came within a whisker of destroying Rome.
text: Then he came within a whisker of destroying Rome.

caption: So here is today's question. Why did Hannibal take the hardest road in the ancient world? And did it work?
text: So here is today's question. Why did Hannibal take the hardest road in the ancient world? And did it work?

caption: Let's follow him on the map.
text: Let's follow him on the map.

caption: First, the grudge. Rome and Carthage were the two great powers of the western Mediterranean.
text: First, the grudge. Rome and Carthage were the two great powers of the western Mediterranean.

caption: From 264 to 241 BC they fought the First Punic War, mostly at sea. Rome won, and Carthage lost Sicily.
text: From two-hundred-sixty-four to two-hundred-forty-one BC they fought the First Punic War, mostly at sea. Rome won, and Carthage lost Sicily.

caption: Carthage had to pay 3,200 talents of silver. Then Rome grabbed Sardinia and Corsica as well, and demanded more.
text: Carthage had to pay three-thousand-two-hundred talents of silver. Then Rome grabbed Sardinia and Corsica as well, and demanded more.

caption: Even Polybius, a Greek historian who admired Rome, called the grab of Sardinia unjust.
text: Even Polybius, a Greek historian who admired Rome, called the grab of Sardinia unjust.

caption: A Carthaginian general, Hamilcar Barca, went west to Spain to build a new empire, rich in silver and soldiers.
text: A Carthaginian general, Hamilcar Barca, went west to Spain to build a new empire, rich in silver and soldiers.

caption: His son-in-law founded a new capital on the Spanish coast: New Carthage. Today, it is Cartagena.
text: His son-in-law founded a new capital on the Spanish coast: New Carthage. Today, it is Cartagena.

caption: The story goes that he made his nine-year-old son swear never to be a friend of Rome. The boy's name was Hannibal.
text: The story goes that he made his nine-year-old son swear never to be a friend of Rome. The boy's name was Hannibal.

caption: In 221 BC, Hannibal took command in Spain. He was about 26.
text: In two-hundred-twenty-one BC, Hannibal took command in Spain. He was about twenty-six.

caption: Two years later he besieged Saguntum, a Spanish city allied to Rome. It fell after eight months.
text: Two years later he besieged Saguntum, a Spanish city allied to Rome. It fell after eight months.

caption: Rome declared war. The Second Punic War had begun.
text: Rome declared war. The Second Punic War had begun.

caption: Rome expected to fight in Spain and in Africa. After all, Rome now ruled the sea.
text: Rome expected to fight in Spain and in Africa. After all, Rome now ruled the sea.

caption: One Roman army headed for Spain. Another gathered in Sicily, ready to sail for Carthage itself.
text: One Roman army headed for Spain. Another gathered in Sicily, ready to sail for Carthage itself.

caption: Hannibal did the one thing nobody expected. He left the sea alone and went by land.
text: Hannibal did the one thing nobody expected. He left the sea alone and went by land.

caption: Polybius puts the route at about 1,600 kilometres. Through Spain, over the Pyrenees, across Gaul, and over the Alps.
text: Polybius puts the route at about one-thousand-six-hundred kilometres. Through Spain, over the Pyrenees, across Gaul, and over the Alps.

caption: Quick quiz. How long did the march from New Carthage to Italy take? Five weeks, five months, or a year?
text: Quick quiz. How long did the march from New Carthage to Italy take? Five weeks, five months, or a year?

caption: Five months. About as long as Napoleon later spent getting to Moscow and back.
text: Five months. About as long as Napoleon later spent getting to Moscow and back.

caption: Polybius says he crossed the Ebro with 90,000 foot soldiers and 12,000 horsemen. Modern historians think that is too many.
text: Polybius says he crossed the Ebro with ninety-thousand foot soldiers and twelve-thousand horsemen. Modern historians think that is too many.

caption: And he brought 37 war elephants.
text: And he brought thirty-seven war elephants.

caption: North of the Ebro, the tribes fought him all the way. He left 11,000 men behind to hold the region, and sent about as many home.
text: North of the Ebro, the tribes fought him all the way. He left eleven-thousand men behind to hold the region, and sent about as many home.

caption: By the time he crossed the Pyrenees, Polybius counts about 50,000 foot and 9,000 horse.
text: By the time he crossed the Pyrenees, Polybius counts about fifty-thousand foot and nine-thousand horse.

caption: In late September he reached the Rhône, a fast, wide river. On the far bank, a Gaulish tribe, the Volcae, was waiting.
text: In late September he reached the Rhône, a fast, wide river. On the far bank, a Gaulish tribe, the Volcae, was waiting.

caption: Hannibal sent a force upstream under an officer named Hanno. They crossed at night on rafts, and came down behind the Gauls.
text: Hannibal sent a force upstream under an officer named Hanno. They crossed at night on rafts, and came down behind the Gauls.

caption: At a smoke signal, the main army crossed. Caught from both sides, the Gauls broke and ran.
text: At a smoke signal, the main army crossed. Caught from both sides, the Gauls broke and ran.

caption: Then the elephants. Hannibal's men built huge rafts and covered them with earth, so the animals thought they were still on land.
text: Then the elephants. Hannibal's men built huge rafts and covered them with earth, so the animals thought they were still on land.

caption: Some elephants panicked and fell into the river. Their drivers drowned, but the elephants swam across.
text: Some elephants panicked and fell into the river. Their drivers drowned, but the elephants swam across.

caption: Meanwhile, a Roman army under the consul Scipio had landed at Massilia to stop him. It reached his camp three days too late.
text: Meanwhile, a Roman army under the consul Scipio had landed at Massilia to stop him. It reached his camp three days too late.

caption: Scipio made a bold call. He sent his army on to Spain under his brother, and hurried back to Italy himself.
card: Army to Spain, he to Italy
text: Scipio made a bold call. He sent his army on to Spain under his brother, and hurried back to Italy himself.

caption: Scipio could not believe it. Hannibal was not heading for Spain or the coast. He was heading for the Alps.
text: Scipio could not believe it. Hannibal was not heading for Spain or the coast. He was heading for the Alps.

caption: Polybius says about 38,000 foot and 8,000 horse left the Rhône. Ahead of them were the Alps, in autumn.
text: Polybius says about thirty-eight-thousand foot and eight-thousand horse left the Rhône. Ahead of them were the Alps, in autumn.

caption: The passes he was heading for are well over 2,000 metres high. One of them is almost 3,000.
text: The passes he was heading for are well over two-thousand metres high. One of them is almost three-thousand.

caption: Mountain tribes, the Allobroges, held the heights above the track, ready to roll rocks down on the column.
text: Mountain tribes, the Allobroges, held the heights above the track, ready to roll rocks down on the column.

caption: He even captured their town, and fed his army from its stores.
text: He even captured their town, and fed his army from its stores.

caption: Hannibal waited for night, when the tribesmen went home to sleep, and quietly took the heights himself.
text: Hannibal waited for night, when the tribesmen went home to sleep, and quietly took the heights himself.

caption: Still, the attacks came. In the narrow gorges, horses and pack animals fell off the cliffs with their loads.
text: Still, the attacks came. In the narrow gorges, horses and pack animals fell off the cliffs with their loads.

caption: The tribes were terrified of the elephants. Wherever the elephants walked, nobody attacked.
text: The tribes were terrified of the elephants. Wherever the elephants walked, nobody attacked.

caption: After nine days they reached the top. Snow had already fallen. It was late October, maybe early November.
text: After nine days they reached the top. Snow had already fallen. It was late October, maybe early November.

caption: The army rested there for two days. Men from Africa and Spain, who had never seen snow, stood freezing on the roof of Europe.
text: The army rested there for two days. Men from Africa and Spain, who had never seen snow, stood freezing on the roof of Europe.

caption: And the way down turned out to be worse than the way up.
text: And the way down turned out to be worse than the way up.

caption: On the Italian side, a landslide had swept the track away. There was no path left. Just a sheer slope of ice and rock.
text: On the Italian side, a landslide had swept the track away. There was no path left. Just a sheer slope of ice and rock.

caption: The men dug a new track into the mountainside. The horses got through after one day.
text: The men dug a new track into the mountainside. The horses got through after one day.

caption: The elephants waited three days, half-starved, before the road was wide enough.
text: The elephants waited three days, half-starved, before the road was wide enough.

caption: Livy, writing 200 years later, says they cracked the rock with fire and vinegar. Polybius, the older source, never mentions it.
text: Livy, writing two-hundred years later, says they cracked the rock with fire and vinegar. Polybius, the older source, never mentions it.

caption: And which pass did they cross? Nobody knows. At least five passes have their supporters.
text: And which pass did they cross? Nobody knows. At least five passes have their supporters.

caption: In 2016, scientists found a layer of ancient horse dung below the Col de la Traversette, dated to around 200 BC. Interesting, but not proof.
text: In twenty-sixteen, scientists found a layer of ancient horse dung below the Col de la Traversette, dated to around two-hundred BC. Interesting, but not proof.

caption: But that date could be sixty years off, and no Carthaginian objects were found there. The mystery is still open.
text: But that date could be sixty years off, and no Carthaginian objects were found there. The mystery is still open.

caption: A 2026 study modelled how much energy each route would cost, and also picked the Traversette. Other historians are not convinced.
text: A twenty-twenty-six study modelled how much energy each route would cost, and also picked the Traversette. Other historians are not convinced.

caption: Quiz time. How many of the 37 elephants made it over the Alps? None, about half, or most of them?
text: Quiz time. How many of the thirty-seven elephants made it over the Alps? None, about half, or most of them?

caption: Most of them. Despite the legend, the elephants survived the Alps. It was what came next that killed them.
text: Most of them. Despite the legend, the elephants survived the Alps. It was what came next that killed them.

caption: Hannibal reached the plains of northern Italy with 20,000 foot and 6,000 horse. We know, because he carved the numbers in bronze himself.
text: Hannibal reached the plains of northern Italy with twenty-thousand foot and six-thousand horse. We know, because he carved the numbers in bronze himself.

caption: In fifteen days in the Alps, he had lost about half the army that left the Rhône. Many deserted. Many died.
text: In fifteen days in the Alps, he had lost about half the army that left the Rhône. Many deserted. Many died.

caption: Rome was stunned. In November, at the Ticinus river, Hannibal's cavalry routed the Romans. The consul Scipio was wounded.
text: Rome was stunned. In November, at the Ticinus river, Hannibal's cavalry routed the Romans. The consul Scipio was wounded.

caption: In December, at the Trebia, he lured about 40,000 Romans across an icy river and ambushed them. Only about 10,000 broke out.
text: In December, at the Trebia, he lured about forty-thousand Romans across an icy river and ambushed them. Only about ten-thousand broke out.

caption: His brother Mago had hidden 2,000 men in a stream bed. When the Romans had crossed, they struck from behind.
text: His brother Mago had hidden two-thousand men in a stream bed. When the Romans had crossed, they struck from behind.

caption: But the winter that followed killed every elephant but one.
text: But the winter that followed killed every elephant but one.

caption: In the spring, Hannibal rode that last elephant through flooded marshes. He caught an infection there, and lost the sight of one eye.
text: In the spring, Hannibal rode that last elephant through flooded marshes. He caught an infection there, and lost the sight of one eye.

caption: In June 217 BC, at Lake Trasimene, he hid his army in the hills. A Roman army marched along the shore, into the morning fog.
text: In June two-hundred-seventeen BC, at Lake Trasimene, he hid his army in the hills. A Roman army marched along the shore, into the morning fog.

caption: About 15,000 Romans were killed in a few hours, including the consul Flaminius.
text: About fifteen-thousand Romans were killed in a few hours, including the consul Flaminius.

caption: Rome panicked. It gave power to Fabius Maximus, who refused to fight a battle at all. He just followed Hannibal and wore him down.
text: Rome panicked. It gave power to Fabius Maximus, who refused to fight a battle at all. He just followed Hannibal and wore him down.

caption: Romans mocked him as the Delayer. By the next summer they wanted a real battle, and a big army to win it.
text: Romans mocked him as the Delayer. By the next summer they wanted a real battle, and a big army to win it.

caption: On the 2nd of August 216 BC, at Cannae, about 86,000 Romans faced Hannibal's 50,000.
text: On the second of August two-hundred-sixteen BC, at Cannae, about eighty-six-thousand Romans faced Hannibal's fifty-thousand.

caption: Hannibal put his weakest troops in the centre, bulging forward like a crescent, and his best African troops on the wings.
text: Hannibal put his weakest troops in the centre, bulging forward like a crescent, and his best African troops on the wings.

caption: The Romans smashed into the centre. It slowly gave way, and pulled them in.
text: The Romans smashed into the centre. It slowly gave way, and pulled them in.

caption: Then the African wings turned inward, and Hannibal's cavalry came round behind. The Romans were surrounded.
text: Then the African wings turned inward, and Hannibal's cavalry came round behind. The Romans were surrounded.

caption: Polybius says about 70,000 Romans died that day. Livy says about 48,000. Either way, it was one of the worst defeats in history.
text: Polybius says about seventy-thousand Romans died that day. Livy says about forty-eight-thousand. Either way, it was one of the worst defeats in history.

caption: One of the two consuls, Aemilius Paullus, died on the field. Rome had lost three armies in under two years.
text: One of the two consuls, Aemilius Paullus, died on the field. Rome had lost three armies in under two years.

caption: Livy says one of Hannibal's officers told him: you know how to win a victory, Hannibal, but not how to use it.
text: Livy says one of Hannibal's officers told him: you know how to win a victory, Hannibal, but not how to use it.

caption: So, did the hardest road work?
text: So, did the hardest road work?

caption: As a surprise, yes. The Alps let Hannibal skip Rome's navy and land an army in Italy that nobody was ready for.
text: As a surprise, yes. The Alps let Hannibal skip Rome's navy and land an army in Italy that nobody was ready for.

caption: But it came at a price. Half his army and almost all his elephants. And no siege engines to take Rome's walls.
text: But it came at a price. Half his army and almost all his elephants. And no siege engines to take Rome's walls.

caption: Hannibal never besieged Rome. Rome refused to surrender, raised new armies, and kept him busy in Italy for fifteen years.
text: Hannibal never besieged Rome. Rome refused to surrender, raised new armies, and kept him busy in Italy for fifteen years.

caption: He had no siege engines, few reinforcements from home, and most of Rome's allies in central Italy stayed loyal.
text: He had no siege engines, few reinforcements from home, and most of Rome's allies in central Italy stayed loyal.

caption: In 203 BC Carthage called him home. A year later, at Zama, a Roman general named Scipio, the son of the consul at the Rhône, beat him.
text: In two-hundred-three BC Carthage called him home. A year later, at Zama, a Roman general named Scipio, the son of the consul at the Rhône, beat him.

caption: Years later, in exile and about to be handed over to Rome, Hannibal took poison.
text: Years later, in exile and about to be handed over to Rome, Hannibal took poison.

caption: Rome won the war. But generals still study Cannae today, and the road over the Alps is still the most famous march in history.
text: Rome won the war. But generals still study Cannae today, and the road over the Alps is still the most famous march in history.
